extraction.notes: No items. The Labor rights section (pages 16-21) contains no material on foreign workers, employment of foreigners, worker mobility between countries or social security across borders; a search of the whole text for foreign, migrant, permit, emigration, Open Balkan, seasonal and residence found none in this section. The section covers cost of living and poverty, wages and trade union protests, the drafting of a new Law on Labor Relations (definition of employee, non-discrimination, equal pay, self-employment), the 2023 amendments for the Bechtel and Enka motorway project and the Helsinki Committee's constitutional initiative, free legal aid, State Labor Inspectorate supervision and the length of labour disputes. This is labour law and social policy (Chapter 19), outside Chapter 2, so not extracted. Technology mentions are incidental: publication of the draft law on the Unified National Electronic Register of Regulations (page 19) and salaries 'published on the web' as a transparency example (page 18). The register note for this source ('Labour rights section on foreign workers') does not match the content. Revised under rules 0.2 and themes 1.1 on 29 October 2026: header updated only; still no items, as the section remains outside the Chapter 2 boundary set in the run record. Revised under rules 0.3 and themes 1.2 on 29 October 2026: header updated only; still no items. Revised under rules 0.4 and themes 1.3 on 30 October 2026 for full extraction: status set to complete; still no items, and no item ID has ever been issued for this source. The Digital rights and freedoms section (page 42), not read in the samples, was now read: it describes only the Committee's own priorities and its project 'Creating a Safer Digital Environment for Young People', which teaches safe internet use (digital skills not linked to an in-scope recommendation), and makes no claim about digital policy, data protection or systems in North Macedonia. The hate speech section (pages 43-46) refers to the online reporting platform, to social networks and to the Commission's lack of a mechanism for finding the address of online perpetrators: these concern hate speech enforcement, so the online references are incidental. 'Electronic communication' in the criminal code amendments on harassment (page 28) and the free legal aid database are also incidental. The only 'foreign' hit in the screen is a physical attack on a foreign individual (hate crime, not workers' rights). The rest of the report covers human rights topics outside the run scope and was not read line by line. The register note still says page 42 was not read; that part is now out of date. Second-pass check done (G3 condition 2).
